q: In which year did the prize go to two architects who did not work together?
o: 2001 — Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron
n: In 1988 the jury honoured Bunshaft and Niemeyer independently. 2001 and 2010 went to partnerships, and Piano and Rogers won in different years.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which laureate, with no formal architectural training, was once a professional boxer?
n: Tadao Ando taught himself architecture by travelling and reading after a boxing career. Ban, Ito and Tange were all university-trained.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who is the youngest person to receive the Pritzker Prize?
n: Ryue Nishizawa was in his early forties when SANAA won in 2010. Aravena was 48 in 2016.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which laureate is famous for working as a sole practitioner, with no staff office?
n: Glenn Murcutt designs alone, mostly houses in Australia. Zumthor keeps a small studio in Haldenstein, but it is still a staffed office.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which laureate died just before his prize was made public, the only one honoured after his death?
n: Frei Otto learned of the 2015 prize before he died in March 2015, and the announcement was brought forward. Hadid, Utzon and Niemeyer all died years after winning.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize?
n: Zaha Hadid won alone in 2004. Kazuyo Sejima became the second woman in 2010, sharing the prize with Ryue Nishizawa.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which was the first group of three architects to win the Pritzker Prize together?
n: Rafael Aranda, Carme Pigem and Ramon Vilalta of Olot, Spain, won together in 2017. Every earlier shared prize went to a pair.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Wang Shu's 2012 prize did not name which co-founder of his Amateur Architecture Studio?
n: Lu Wenyu co-founded Amateur Architecture Studio with Wang Shu, her husband, but the prize went to him alone, as with Scott Brown and Venturi in 1991.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the second woman to receive the Pritzker Prize?
n: Kazuyo Sejima of SANAA won in 2010. Carme Pigem (2017), Farrell and McNamara (2020) and Anne Lacaton (2021) came later.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who were the first two women to share the Pritzker Prize?
o: Denise Scott Brown and Lu Wenyu
n: The Irish founders of Grafton Architects won in 2020. Every other shared prize included at least one man.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Whose exclusion from Robert Venturi's 1991 prize prompted a 2013 petition that the jury declined?
n: Scott Brown was Venturi's wife and design partner, but the 1991 prize named only him. The 2013 petition asked for her retroactive inclusion and was turned down.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which firm was the first to receive the prize as a partnership of two architects?
n: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron were honoured jointly in 2001. SANAA followed in 2010, Grafton in 2020, and Lacaton & Vassal in 2021.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Besides a bronze medallion, what does a Pritzker laureate receive?
n: The award is a US$100,000 grant plus a bronze medallion. It is modest in cash compared with its prestige.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which foundation, tied to a hotel chain, sponsors the Pritzker Prize?
n: The Pritzkers owned Hyatt Hotels, and the prize is run through the Hyatt Foundation.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which three words, from Vitruvius, appear on the Pritzker medallion?
n: The medallion quotes Vitruvius's firmitas, utilitas, venustas in Sir Henry Wotton's English: firmness, commodity and delight.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: The Pritzker Architecture Prize was founded in 1979 by which couple?
o: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur
n: Jay A. Pritzker and his wife Cindy established the prize in 1979, funded through the family's Hyatt Foundation. The Pritzker family owned the Hyatt hotel chain.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: What does the Pritzker Prize recognise?
o: A lifetime of architectural writing and teaching
A single outstanding building from the past year
The best unbuilt design competition entry
A living architect's built work over a career
n: The prize honours a living architect whose built work shows a significant, consistent contribution to humanity and the built environment. No single project wins it.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: The Pritzker is popularly compared to which other award?
n: The prize was modelled on the Nobel in scope and jury process, and the press routinely calls it "architecture's Nobel".
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which two laureates designed the Centre Pompidou together, then won the prize in separate years?
o: Jean Nouvel and Christian de Portzamparc
n: Piano and Rogers won the 1971 Pompidou competition as partners. Piano won the prize in 1998 and Rogers in 2007. Foster and Rogers were partners too, earlier, in Team 4.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which Portuguese laureate worked in Álvaro Siza's office early in his career?
n: Souto de Moura worked with Siza (1992) in Porto before winning himself in 2011. The two also designed the 2005 Serpentine Pavilion together.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Zaha Hadid studied under, and later worked for, which laureate?
n: Hadid was Koolhaas's student at the Architectural Association in London and joined his firm OMA. Koolhaas won in 2000 and Hadid in 2004.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Kazuyo Sejima worked in which future laureate's office before founding SANAA?
n: Sejima worked for Toyo Ito before starting her own firm. She won in 2010, three years before Ito did in 2013.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which laureate trained and worked under Kenzo Tange before winning the prize himself?
n: Arata Isozaki worked for Kenzo Tange (1987 laureate) before starting his own practice, and won in 2019.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which two British laureates were partners in the 1960s practice Team 4?
n: Foster and Rogers founded Team 4 in 1963 with Su Brumwell and Wendy Cheesman. Foster won in 1999 and Rogers in 2007.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first Japanese architect to win the Pritzker Prize?
n: Kenzo Tange won in 1987. Maki followed in 1993 and Ando in 1995. Isozaki, who began in Tange's office, won much later, in 2019.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first-ever Pritzker laureate, in 1979?
n: Philip Johnson won the inaugural prize in 1979. Luis Barragán followed in 1980, then James Stirling in 1981.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first Chinese citizen to win the Pritzker Prize?
n: Wang Shu won in 2012. I. M. Pei (1983) was born in China but was an American citizen. Liu Jiakun became the second Chinese laureate in 2025.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Which two Chilean architects have won the Pritzker Prize?
o: Alejandro Aravena and Smiljan Radić Clarke
Alejandro Aravena and Paulo Mendes da Rocha
Smiljan Radić Clarke and Luis Barragán
n: Aravena won in 2016 and Radić in 2026. Mendes da Rocha is Brazilian and Barragán Mexican. Mathias Klotz is Chilean but not a laureate.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first Brazilian Pritzker laureate?
n: Oscar Niemeyer won in 1988. Paulo Mendes da Rocha became the second Brazilian in 2006. Lina Bo Bardi never received the prize.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first Latin American to win the Pritzker Prize?
n: Mexico's Luis Barragán won in 1980, only the second year of the prize. Niemeyer, the first Brazilian, came in 1988.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first Australian to win the Pritzker Prize?
n: Glenn Murcutt won in 2002. Jørn Utzon, who won the next year, is Danish even though his best-known work is the Sydney Opera House.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first African, and first Black, Pritzker laureate?
n: Burkina Faso's Francis Kéré won in 2022. David Adjaye is a well-known African-born architect who has not received the prize.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)

q: Who was the first Indian architect to win the Pritzker Prize?
n: Balkrishna Doshi won in 2018. Charles Correa, often named as a contender, never received it.
ref: Pritzker Architecture Prize — Laureates list and prize history (pritzkerprize.com)
